cshell as a lightweighter

Study report · 2026-11-10 · branch worktree-cshell-lightweight · draft PR #4

Result. cshell now defaults to objective.type = "lightweight". It minimises mass subject to stiffness and load capacity both at least those of the original solid. All 7 designs accepted in this study meet K/K0 ≥ 1 and P/P0 ≥ 1 on both the optimisation grid and the shifted re-score grid. The savings are 2.4–14.9 % on the three existing examples, which are already slender and thin-membered, and 30–50 % on stocky parts. The old constant-mass optimiser remains available as objective.type = "weighted", with its behaviour unchanged.

49.5 %best saving (stocky beam 24×24×160)
30.2 %non-beam part (bell crank)
14.9 %best existing example (MBB)
7 / 8runs accepted (both grids, K and P ≥ 1)

1. Formulation

The previous default kept the mass fixed and traded stiffness K against capacity P. Capacity P is a soft-min of the strength p-norm and global linear buckling, and both K and P are measured relative to the solid. The lightweighter reverses the roles of objective and constraint:

minimise   f₀ = (V/V₀) / s          (s = constraint scale; no mass restoration step)
subject to ln K/K₀ ≥ ln 1.02,   ln P/P₀ ≥ ln 1.02      (MMA constraints)
           t ≥ t_min, voids ≥ v_min, as-built biases, passive mounts, closure skirt (unchanged)
  • Margin. The optimiser constrains K/K0 and P/P0 to at least 1.02. The 2 % margin absorbs the error between the optimisation grid and the shifted re-score grid. Acceptance requires K/K0 ≥ 1 and P/P0 ≥ 1 on both grids, plus a positive mass saving. The largest observed drop from the 1.02 constraint to the shifted grid was to 1.018, so 1.02 is sufficient.
  • Start point. The optimiser starts from the solid, which has K/K0 = P/P0 = 1. This is slightly infeasible against the 1.02 constraints, and MMA recovers by moving walls outward.
  • Objective scaling. In the first attempt, MBB ended with K/K0 = 0.990 and the solid was kept. The reason was the size of the mass objective, which reused the weighted mode's scaling. It was about 104 per 1 % of mass, while MMA's elastic penalty was only about 103 per 1 % of constraint violation. Because the penalty was smaller, violating the stiffness constraint was "cheaper" for MMA than adding mass back. The fix (commit 5d0375e) scales f₀ in constraint units so that feasibility dominates. All runs were repeated after the fix.
  • Downstream changes.
    • The growth schedule's "best boundary" is now the lowest-mass boundary that is feasible.
    • The export mass correction targets Vopt instead of V0.
    • The summary and report label the result as a mass saving.

Stiffness is the limiting constraint in every case: K/K0 ends at its 1.02 constraint value, while P often has spare capacity. These parts are already slender and thin-membered, with little low-stress core to remove. The constant-mass runs show this too. Cantilever could not even hold K at constant mass (0.975), so any gram removed must be bought back by moving section outward, and the saving stays small. Note that the constant-mass Cantilever design would fail the new acceptance rule.

3. Demonstration parts chosen to be lightweighted

Why these parts. In bending, the stress at a point is proportional to its distance y from the neutral axis, and stiffness depends on I = ∫y² dA. Material in the core near the axis therefore carries little load and contributes little stiffness, yet in a stocky solid section it is most of the mass. Hollowing the core and pushing the skin slightly outward restores I, and with it K and the strength capacity, at a fraction of the mass.

For a thin-walled box section, this estimate predicts about 55 % saving at mid-span. The solid ends, mounts and load pads reduce the achievable saving below that. Buckling does not limit these parts, because for the solids the buckling capacity is about 10× the strength capacity (λb0/λs0 ≈ 10).

The solids were generated as new STEP files: make_demo.py for the beams and make_bellcrank.py for the bell crank. They were run with cshell defaults, changing only mounts.auto_analytic=false. That change is needed because a CAD-generated solid has only analytic faces, so auto-detection would otherwise mark every face as a mount and leave nothing to design.

Bell crank v1 failed only on the shifted grid. There, the stress peak at the rim of the clamped pivot bore rose by 8 %. A stress concentration at a sharp bore edge depends on the voxel grid, so it was not resolved consistently. Enlarging the boss and adding a fillet removed the concentration, and v2 passed with spare capacity. In this case the acceptance check on the second grid did its job and rejected an under-resolved design.

4. Verification and cost

  • Tests.
    • CPU suite: 196 passed, 34 skipped.
    • GPU suite: 240 passed, plus 18 passed in a rerun of test_objective and test_lightweight. One GPU array task had timed out because it also ran slow CPU variants.
    • New tests in tests/cshell/test_lightweight.py cover the constraint set, the absence of mass restoration, a gradient check of f₀, best-boundary selection, the export target and the decision rule.
    • Tests and bench configs that need constant mass now pin objective.type="weighted".
  • Checks on every design.
    • A shifted-grid re-score.
    • A 0.2 mm watertight export, mass-matched to Vopt.
    • Walls ≥ tmin (1.5 mm nominal; the minimum measured on the exported mesh was 1.44 mm, on the Cantilever).
  • Cost.
    • One GH200 GPU per part.
    • Existing examples: 29–38 min each, with peak memory of 13–26 GiB on the GPU and 17–31 GiB on the host.
    • Demo parts: 35–52 min each, with peak host memory of 45–52 GB. The longest beam needed one automatic continuation job.
    • Requests were --gpus=1 --time=01:15:00 with 8–16 CPUs. Note that workq allocates 115 GB of memory per GPU regardless of --mem.

5. Limitations

  • Voxel validation only. Acceptance rests on voxel FE criteria on two grids. Body-fitted (C3D10) validation is still not run at this scale, as before.
  • Fixed margin. The 1.02 margin is fixed in config (objective.lw_margin_stiffness, lw_margin_capacity). It could be lowered toward 1.01 for slightly more saving. Bell crank v1 shows that the second-grid check, not the margin, is what catches under-resolved stress peaks.
  • Mount detection. CAD-generated parts need mounts.auto_analytic=false, which is worth handling automatically in future.

6. Use

# lightweight (new default)
cshell/cluster/launch_part.sh examples/cshell/<part>.json
# previous constant-mass weighted optimiser
cshell/cluster/launch_part.sh examples/cshell/<part>.json --set objective.type=weighted
